newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sells 3.879 bln reais in Central Bank Bonds.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sells 3.879 bln reais in Central Bank Bonds.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank sold 3.879 billion reais in 56-day Central Bank Bonds (BBC) at its weekly formal bond auction Tuesday, dealers said.
The Central Bank sold the bonds at an overnight rate of 2.428 percent a month, up from 2.42 percent last week.

The Central Bank did not accept offers for 1.5 billion reais in 182-day BBCs. Traders said the Bank's refusal reflected its fears that offers on the longer-dated paper would result in higher interest rates on those bonds.

The Central Bank did not want to signal a higher interest rate scenario to the market, traders said. They said such a belief had developed in the market following the Central Bank's decision two weeks ago to leave interest rates alone, reversing an eight-month policy of cutting rates.

In addition, the Central Bank's decision last week to lower taxes on foreign investment to attract more short-term capital flows suggested the government was worried about international reserve levels and that the policy of gradual interest rate declines may have come to an end.
Prior to the auction, most players thought the 182-day BBC auction would come in at 2.47 percent, up from the result of the last auction, when the Central Bank sold 182-day BBC at 2.377 percent.
The financial result of the auction indicated 1.621 billion reais will be added to the banking system as 5.5 billion reais in 56-day old bonds are coming due Wednesday.
